questions.stem: What is the sum of the digits of the year 2038?
questions.solution: The digits are 2, 0, 3 and 8. Their sum is 2 + 0 + 3 + 8 = 13.

questions.stem: Ines has four digit cards: 3, 0, 7 and 5. She uses all four cards once to make the largest possible number. Which number does she make?
questions.solution: Put the biggest digit first, then the next biggest, and so on: 7, 5, 3, 0. The number is 7530.

questions.stem: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 6 and 2 exactly once to make the smallest possible four-digit number. A number cannot start with 0. What is the number?
questions.solution: The first digit cannot be 0, so the smallest choice is 2. Then use 0, then 4, then 6. The number is 2046.

questions.stem: In the sum 5? + 38 = 91, the question mark hides one digit. Which digit is it?
questions.solution: 91 - 38 = 53, so the two-digit number is 53. The hidden digit is 3.

questions.stem: In the number 685, what is the value of the digit 8?
questions.solution: The digit 8 is in the tens place, so it stands for 8 tens, which is 80.

questions.stem: Tomas writes the numbers 325, 235, 352 and 253 in a list from the biggest to the smallest. Which number is third in the list?
questions.solution: From biggest to smallest the list is 352, 325, 253, 235. The third number is 253.

questions.stem: What number is 10 more than 395?
questions.solution: Adding 10 to 395 gives 405, because 9 tens and 1 more ten make 10 tens, which carries.

questions.stem: Three boxes are in a row. The first box holds 8. The second box holds 5 more than the first. The third box holds double the second. What number is in the third box?
questions.solution: The second box holds 8 + 5 = 13. The third box holds 2 times 13, which is 26.

questions.stem: A three-digit number has the digit 4 in the hundreds place and the digit 6 in the ones place. The sum of its three digits is 12. What is the number?
questions.solution: The tens digit is 12 - 4 - 6 = 2. The number is 426.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers has a digit sum of exactly 12?
questions.solution: 5 + 7 = 12. The other numbers have digit sums 11, 13 and 14.

questions.stem: Which is the first year after 2027 whose digits add up to 5?
questions.solution: The years 2028 and 2029 have digit sums 12 and 13. The year 2030 has 2 + 0 + 3 + 0 = 5. So the answer is 2030.

questions.stem: The same digit is written in both gaps: ?4 + 4? = 99. Which digit is it?
questions.solution: Try 5: 54 + 45 = 99. Digits 4, 6 and 7 give 88, 110 and 121 instead.

questions.stem: Five boxes stand in a row. The numbers in any three boxes next to each other add up to 21. The first box holds 5 and the second box holds 9. What number is in the fifth box?
questions.solution: The third box holds 21 - 5 - 9 = 7. The fourth box holds 21 - 9 - 7 = 5. The fifth box holds 21 - 7 - 5 = 9.

questions.stem: Kasi has digit cards 1, 9 and 4. She makes the largest three-digit number and the smallest three-digit number using all three cards each time. What is the difference between them?
questions.solution: The largest number is 941 and the smallest is 149. The difference is 941 - 149 = 792.

questions.stem: Kofi numbers the pages of his diary from 1 to 30. How many times does he write the digit 2 in all?
questions.solution: Digit 2 appears in the ones place of 2, 12 and 22, which is 3 times. It appears in the tens place of 20 to 29, which is 10 times. Altogether 13 times.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers has the biggest digit sum?
questions.solution: The digit sums are 18 for 99, 10 for 190, 9 for 207 and 17 for 386. The biggest is 18, for 99.

questions.stem: In the sum 3?6 + 25 = 401, the question mark hides one digit. Which digit is it?
questions.solution: 401 - 25 = 376. So the hidden digit is 7.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers have a digit sum of 4?
questions.solution: The numbers are 13, 22, 31 and 40. That is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: Zara thinks of a number. She adds 8, doubles the result and then subtracts 6. She gets 30. Which number did she think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards: 30 + 6 = 36, half of 36 is 18, and 18 - 8 = 10.

questions.stem: Pedro has three digit cards: 0, 2 and 5. He uses all three cards to make three-digit numbers. A number cannot start with 0. How many different numbers can he make?
questions.solution: The numbers are 205, 250, 502 and 520. That is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: A two-digit number is added to the number with its digits swapped. The result is 154. The tens digit of the first number is 2 more than its ones digit. What is the first number?
questions.solution: The two digits add up to 14, because 154 = 11 times 14. Digits that add up to 14 and differ by 2 are 8 and 6. The tens digit is bigger, so the number is 86. Check: 86 + 68 = 154.

questions.stem: What is the smallest four-digit number whose digits are all different and add up to 10?
questions.solution: Start with 1 and then 0 to keep the number small. The last two digits must add to 9 and be different and not 0 or 1. The smallest tens digit is 2, so the last digit is 7. The number is 1027.

solve.work: Start 10, last two distinct summing to 9 avoiding 0,1: 27 smallest; 1009/1126 repeat digits.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 contain the digit 7 at least once?
questions.solution: The numbers 7, 17, 27, ..., 97 are 10 numbers. The numbers 70 to 79 are 10 more, but 77 is in both lists. So there are 10 + 10 - 1 = 19 numbers.

solve.work: 10 with units 7 + 10 in the 70s - 77 counted twice.

questions.stem: Lena writes the page numbers from 1 to 100, one after another. How many digits does she write altogether?
questions.solution: Pages 1 to 9 use 9 digits. Pages 10 to 99 are 90 numbers with 2 digits, which is 180 digits. Page 100 uses 3 digits. In all 9 + 180 + 3 = 192.

questions.stem: A triangle has a circle at each corner and a circle in the middle of each side. The number in a side circle is the sum of the numbers in the two corner circles at the ends of that side. The three side circles hold 9, 11 and 14. What is the biggest number in a corner circle?
questions.solution: Adding the three side numbers counts every corner twice: 9 + 11 + 14 = 34, so the three corners add up to 17. The corner opposite the side with 9 is 17 - 9 = 8. The other corners are 17 - 11 = 6 and 17 - 14 = 3. The biggest is 8.

questions.stem: Use each of the digits 2, 4, 6 and 8 exactly once to write two two-digit numbers. What is the largest possible sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: To make the sum big, put the two biggest digits in the tens places: 8 and 6. The ones places get 4 and 2. For example 84 + 62 = 146.

questions.stem: A three-digit number has 0 as its tens digit. Its digits add up to 9. Its hundreds digit is twice its ones digit. Which number is it?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit and ones digit add to 9, and the hundreds digit is double the ones digit. So the ones digit is 3 and the hundreds digit is 6. The number is 603.

questions.stem: How many years from 2000 to 2099 (both included) have a digit sum of 6?
questions.solution: The years are 20ab with a + b = 4. The pairs are 04, 13, 22, 31 and 40. So the years are 2004, 2013, 2022, 2031 and 2040: 5 years.

questions.stem: Mika writes a list of numbers. The first number is 19. Each next number is the number before it plus its digit sum. The list begins 19, 29, 40, ... What is the fifth number in the list?
questions.solution: Third number 40; its digit sum is 4, so the fourth is 44. The digit sum of 44 is 8, so the fifth is 44 + 8 = 52.

questions.stem: A two-digit number is 6 times the sum of its digits. What is the number?
questions.solution: Call the digits tens T and ones U. Then 10T + U = 6T + 6U, so 4T = 5U. The only digits that work are T = 5 and U = 4. The number is 54, and 6 times 9 is 54.

questions.stem: Anna buys 3 notebooks that cost 6 euros each. She pays with a 20-euro note. How many euros of change does she get?
questions.solution: The notebooks cost 3 times 6 = 18 euros. The change is 20 - 18 = 2 euros.

questions.stem: A box holds 8 cookies. Sam has 5 full boxes. He eats 7 cookies. How many cookies are left?
questions.solution: There are 5 times 8 = 40 cookies. After eating 7 there are 40 - 7 = 33.

questions.stem: There are 20 children in the club. A quarter of them ride a bike to the club. How many do NOT ride a bike?
questions.solution: A quarter of 20 is 5, so 5 ride a bike. The other 20 - 5 = 15 do not.

questions.stem: Mia reads 12 pages on Monday, 9 pages on Tuesday and 14 pages on Wednesday. How many pages does she read in the three days?
17 sweets are shared equally among 5 children. Each child gets as many as possible. How many sweets are left over?
questions.solution: Each child gets 3 sweets, which uses 15. So 17 - 15 = 2 sweets are left over.

questions.stem: Tina has 37 stickers. She wants to have 60. How many more stickers does she need?
questions.solution: 60 - 37 = 23 stickers.

questions.stem: A sandwich costs 5 euros and a juice costs 2 euros. Ben buys 2 sandwiches and 1 juice. How many euros does he pay?
questions.solution: Two sandwiches cost 10 euros. Add 2 euros for the juice. The total is 12 euros.

questions.stem: There are 14 birds in a tree. Half of them fly away, then 3 more birds land in the tree. How many birds are in the tree now?
questions.solution: Half of 14 is 7. Then 7 + 3 = 10 birds.

questions.stem: Eggs are sold in boxes of 6. Pia needs at least 20 eggs. What is the smallest number of boxes she must buy?
questions.solution: Three boxes hold 18 eggs, which is not enough. Four boxes hold 24 eggs. So she needs 4 boxes.

questions.stem: A shop sells 15 loaves of bread on Saturday. On Sunday it sells twice as many as on Saturday. How many loaves does it sell on the two days together?
questions.solution: On Sunday it sells 30 loaves. Together 15 + 30 = 45 loaves.

questions.stem: Buns are sold in bags of 3 and bags of 5. Hugo wants exactly 14 buns. What is the smallest number of bags he can buy?
questions.solution: Three bags hold at most 15 buns, and with sizes 3 and 5 the totals are 9, 11, 13 or 15, never 14. With four bags, 5 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 14. So the smallest number is 4.

solve.work: 14=5+3+3+3; 2 or 3 bags cannot make 14 (max 15 with 3 bags only as 5+5+5).

questions.stem: Marta has 30 beads. She makes as many bracelets as she can with 7 beads in each. How many beads are left over?
questions.solution: Four bracelets use 28 beads. So 30 - 28 = 2 beads are left.

questions.stem: Omar buys 2 books that cost 9 euros each and a pen that costs 4 euros. He pays with a 30-euro note. How many euros of change does he get?
questions.solution: The books cost 18 euros, so with the pen he pays 22 euros. The change is 30 - 22 = 8 euros.

questions.stem: A third of Lena's marbles are green. She has 6 green marbles. She gives away 5 marbles that are not green. How many marbles does she have now?
questions.solution: Six is a third of her marbles, so she has 18. After giving 5 away she has 18 - 5 = 13.

questions.stem: 29 children go on a trip. Each minibus takes at most 8 children. What is the smallest number of minibuses needed?
questions.solution: Three minibuses carry 24 children, which is not enough. Four carry 32. So 4 minibuses are needed.

questions.stem: Kai saves 3 euros each day for 9 days. Then he buys a toy that costs 20 euros. How many euros does he have left?
questions.solution: In 9 days he saves 27 euros. After the toy he has 27 - 20 = 7 euros.

questions.stem: A ticket costs 6 euros for an adult. A child pays half of that. A family buys tickets for 2 adults and 3 children. How many euros do they pay?
questions.solution: Two adults pay 12 euros. A child ticket costs 3 euros, so three children pay 9 euros. The total is 12 + 9 = 21 euros.

questions.stem: A class has 28 children. A quarter of them walk to school and half of them come by bus. The rest come by car. How many children come by car?
questions.solution: A quarter of 28 is 7 and half of 28 is 14. So 28 - 7 - 14 = 7 children come by car.

questions.stem: On the first day Nadia reads 4 pages. Each next day she reads 2 pages more than the day before. How many pages does she read in 5 days altogether?
questions.solution: The five days are 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 pages. Their sum is 40.

questions.stem: A book has 120 pages. Sam reads 35 pages on Monday and 48 pages on Tuesday. How many more pages must he read to finish the book?
questions.solution: He has read 35 + 48 = 83 pages. So 120 - 83 = 37 pages remain.

questions.stem: Candy is sold in boxes of 5, 9 and 12 pieces. Rosa wants exactly 47 pieces. What is the smallest number of boxes she can buy?
questions.solution: Four boxes cannot make 47 whichever sizes are used (all sums with four boxes of these sizes miss 47). Five boxes work: 12 + 12 + 9 + 9 + 5 = 47. So the answer is 5.

solve.work: No 4-box combination of 5/9/12 makes 47 (checked by count of 5s); 12+12+9+9+5=47.

questions.stem: One jar of jam costs 4 euros. A bundle of 3 jars costs 10 euros. Pia wants exactly 8 jars. What is the smallest number of euros she can pay?
questions.solution: Two bundles give 6 jars for 20 euros, and 2 single jars cost 8 euros: 28 euros in all. One bundle and 5 single jars cost 30, and 8 single jars cost 32. The cheapest is 28.

solve.work: 2 bundles + 2 singles = 20+8=28 (3 bundles give 9 jars, not exactly 8).

questions.stem: Three children share 36 stickers. Dana takes half of them and Eli takes a third of them. Fay gets all the others. How many stickers does Fay get?
questions.solution: Dana gets 18 and Eli gets 12. Fay gets 36 - 18 - 12 = 6 stickers.

questions.stem: At a show, an adult ticket costs 5 euros and a child ticket costs 3 euros. A group of 7 people pays 29 euros in all. How many children are in the group?
questions.solution: If all 7 paid 3 euros it would be 21 euros. The real total is 8 euros more, and each adult adds 2 euros, so there are 4 adults and 3 children. Check: 20 + 9 = 29.

questions.stem: Lia spends half of her money on a book. Then she spends 6 euros on lunch. She has 9 euros left. How many euros did she have at the start?
questions.solution: Before lunch she had 9 + 6 = 15 euros. That was half of her money, so at the start she had 30 euros.

questions.stem: Pip plants 3 flowers on the first day. Each next day she plants 2 more flowers than the day before. She does this for 6 days. How many flowers does she plant altogether?
questions.solution: The six days are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13 flowers. The sum is 48.

questions.stem: A tin holds 24 cookies. Tom eats a quarter of them. Then Uma eats a third of the cookies that are left. How many cookies are left in the tin now?
questions.solution: Tom eats 6, so 18 are left. Uma eats a third of 18, which is 6. So 12 cookies are left.

questions.stem: A baker needs 100 rolls. She has baked 3 trays with 12 rolls each and 2 trays with 15 rolls each. How many more rolls must she bake?
questions.solution: The trays give 36 + 30 = 66 rolls. She needs 100 - 66 = 34 more.

questions.stem: Max buys stickers for 2 euros each. For every 4 stickers he buys he gets 1 extra sticker free. He spends 20 euros. How many stickers does he have in all?
questions.solution: With 20 euros he buys 10 stickers. Two groups of 4 stickers bought give 2 free stickers. In all 10 + 2 = 12.

questions.stem: Nora has more than 30 and fewer than 50 stickers. If she puts them in rows of 6, 2 stickers are left over. If she puts them in rows of 5, 3 stickers are left over. How many stickers does she have?
questions.solution: Numbers with 2 left over in sixes are 32, 38, 44 and 50. Of these only 38 has 3 left over in fives (35 + 3). So she has 38 stickers.

solve.work: 2 mod 6 in range: 32, 38, 44; only 38 is 3 mod 5.

questions.stem: Mia is 9 years old. Her brother Tom is 4 years older than Mia. Her sister Zoe is 3 years younger than Mia. How many years older is Tom than Zoe?
questions.solution: Tom is 9 + 4 = 13 and Zoe is 9 - 3 = 6. The difference is 13 - 6 = 7.

questions.stem: A block of cheese balances 4 small apples on a scale. Each small apple weighs 25 grams. How many grams does the cheese weigh?
questions.solution: Four apples weigh 4 times 25 = 100 grams, and the cheese balances them.

questions.skill: two kinds of coin with a total
questions.stem: Kai has 12 coins. Each coin is worth 1 euro or 2 euros. Exactly 7 of the coins are 1-euro coins. How many euros does Kai have in all?
questions.solution: There are 12 - 7 = 5 two-euro coins worth 10 euros. Together with 7 euros that makes 17 euros.

questions.stem: Two equal melons are on one pan of a scale. On the other pan are a 3 kg weight and a 1 kg weight. The scale balances. How many kilograms does one melon weigh?
questions.solution: The weights add up to 4 kg, which the two melons share equally: 2 kg each.

questions.stem: Leo is 8 years old. His father is 4 times as old as Leo. How old will Leo's father be in 2 years?
questions.solution: Father is 8 times 4 = 32 now, so he will be 34 in 2 years.

questions.stem: Five equal boxes weigh 20 kg altogether. How many kilograms do six of these boxes weigh?
questions.solution: One box weighs 20 / 5 = 4 kg, so six boxes weigh 24 kg.

questions.stem: On one pan of a scale are a bag of rice and a 2 kg weight. On the other pan is a 5 kg weight. The scale balances. How many kilograms does the bag of rice weigh?
questions.solution: Taking the 2 kg weight from both sides leaves the bag balancing 3 kg.

questions.stem: In 5 years Sam will be 12 years old. How old was Sam 3 years ago?
questions.solution: Sam is 12 - 5 = 7 now, so 3 years ago he was 4.

questions.stem: A cat weighs as much as 2 rabbits. A dog weighs as much as 3 cats. How many rabbits weigh as much as one dog?
questions.solution: One dog is 3 cats, and each cat is 2 rabbits, so a dog is 3 times 2 = 6 rabbits.

questions.stem: Two equal dolls and a ball that weighs 100 grams together weigh 500 grams. How many grams does one doll weigh?
questions.solution: Without the ball the two dolls weigh 400 grams, so one doll weighs 200 grams.

questions.stem: Ana and Ben have 20 stickers together. Ana has 6 more stickers than Ben. How many stickers does Ana have?
questions.solution: Without Ana's 6 extra stickers, 14 are left, shared equally: 7 each. So Ben has 7 and Ana has 7 + 6 = 13.

questions.stem: Lena and her grandmother have ages that add up to 70. The grandmother is 60 years older than Lena. How old is Lena?
questions.solution: Take away the 60 extra years: 10 years are left, shared equally, so Lena is 5 (and her grandmother 65).

questions.stem: A cone and a ball weigh 9 kg together. A cone and two balls weigh 12 kg together. How many kilograms does the cone weigh?
questions.solution: The second weighing has one more ball, and it is 3 kg heavier, so a ball weighs 3 kg. Then the cone weighs 9 - 3 = 6 kg.

questions.skill: two kinds of coin: guess and check
questions.stem: Pim has 9 coins. Each is a 50-cent coin or a 20-cent coin. Together they are worth 3 dollars. How many 50-cent coins does Pim have?
questions.solution: Try 4 fifty-cent coins: 200 cents, plus 5 twenty-cent coins: 100 cents, gives 300 cents. Each extra 50-cent coin instead of a 20-cent one adds 30 cents, so 4 is the only fit.

questions.stem: Eli and Fay share 28 candies. Eli gets 3 times as many candies as Fay. How many candies does Eli get?
questions.solution: Fay's share is one part and Eli's is three parts, so there are 4 parts: 28 / 4 = 7. Eli gets 3 times 7 = 21.

questions.stem: On a scale, 3 equal jars balance 2 equal bags. One bag weighs 6 kg. How many kilograms does one jar weigh?
questions.solution: Two bags weigh 12 kg, and three jars balance them, so one jar weighs 12 / 3 = 4 kg.

questions.stem: Tomas is 3 years older than Una, and Una is 2 years older than Vik. Their three ages add up to 31. How old is Tomas?
questions.solution: If Vik is v, Una is v + 2 and Tomas is v + 5, so three times v plus 7 is 31. Then v = 8 and Tomas is 13.

solve.work: Vik v, Una v+2, Tomas v+5; 3v+7 = 31, v = 8, Tomas 13.

questions.stem: A melon weighs as much as 3 apples. Two melons and one apple together weigh 700 grams. How many grams does one apple weigh?
questions.solution: Two melons are 6 apples, so the load is 7 apples in all. Then one apple weighs 700 / 7 = 100 grams.

questions.stem: Hana is 3 times as old as her brother Dan. Hana is also 12 years older than Dan. How old is Hana?
questions.solution: The 12 years of difference are 2 times Dan's age, so Dan is 6 and Hana is 18.

questions.stem: Zara thinks of a number, multiplies it by 3, subtracts 4 and gets 20. What was her number?
questions.solution: Undo the steps: 20 + 4 = 24, and 24 / 3 = 8.

questions.stem: A mother is 30 years older than her daughter. In 5 years the mother will be 4 times as old as her daughter. How old is the daughter now?
questions.solution: Try 5: the mother is 35 now. In 5 years they are 40 and 10, and 40 is 4 times 10. Trying 4 gives 39 and 9, which does not work.

questions.stem: A cat and a dog together weigh 11 kg. The dog and a rabbit together weigh 9 kg. The cat and the rabbit together weigh 8 kg. How many kilograms does the dog weigh?
questions.solution: Adding the three weighings counts every animal twice: 28 kg, so all three weigh 14 kg. The dog is 14 - 8 = 6 kg.

solve.work: Sum of all three = 28/2 = 14; dog = 14 - 8 = 6 (cat 5, rabbit 3).

questions.stem: On a scale, 2 equal boxes balance 3 equal bags. One bag balances 4 equal balls. How many balls balance one box?
questions.solution: Three bags are 12 balls, which balance 2 boxes, so one box balances 6 balls.

questions.stem: Four sisters have ages that add up to 48. Each is 2 years older than the next younger sister. How old is the oldest sister?
questions.solution: If the youngest is y, the ages are y, y + 2, y + 4 and y + 6, which add to 4y + 12 = 48. So y = 9 and the oldest is 15.

questions.skill: two kinds with a total: legs
questions.stem: In a garden there are 15 animals, all birds (2 legs each) or rabbits (4 legs each). Together they have 44 legs. How many rabbits are there?
questions.solution: If all 15 were birds there would be 30 legs. Each rabbit adds 2 legs, so 14 extra legs mean 7 rabbits.

solve.work: All birds give 30 legs; extra 14/2 = 7 rabbits, 8 birds.

questions.stem: Maya gave away half of her stickers, then bought 6 more, then gave away one third of what she then had. She now has 8 stickers. How many did she have at the start?
questions.solution: Before the last step she had 12, because 12 minus a third is 8. Before buying 6 she had 6, which was half of her start. So she began with 12.

solve.work: Backwards: 8 is 2/3 of 12; minus 6 = 6; doubled = 12. Check 12->6->12->8.

questions.stem: Jon is 7 years older than Ken. Three years ago Jon was twice as old as Ken. How old is Ken now?
questions.solution: Three years ago the gap was still 7, and Jon was twice Ken, so Ken was 7 then. Now Ken is 10.

solve.work: K+7-3 = 2(K-3) -> K = 10; Jon 17, three years ago 14 and 7.

questions.stem: 3 oranges and 2 lemons weigh 480 grams. 1 orange and 2 lemons weigh 280 grams. How many grams does one lemon weigh?
questions.solution: The difference is 2 oranges = 200 grams, so an orange is 100 grams. Then 2 lemons weigh 180 grams and one lemon 90 grams.

questions.stem: Ada, Bea and Cai share 50 marbles. Ada gets twice as many as Bea, and Bea gets three times as many as Cai. How many marbles does Ada get?
questions.solution: Cai has one part, Bea 3 parts and Ada 6 parts: 10 parts in all, so a part is 5. Ada gets 30.

questions.stem: Two big stones weigh as much as five small stones. One big stone and six small stones together weigh 17 kg. How many kilograms does one big stone weigh?
questions.solution: A big stone is worth 2.5 small ones, so the load is 8.5 small stones = 17 kg. A small stone is 2 kg and a big stone 5 kg.

questions.stem: A row of numbers starts 7, 12, 17, 22, and keeps adding the same amount each time. What is the 8th number in the row?
questions.solution: The step is 5. From the 1st number to the 8th there are 7 steps, so the 8th number is 7 + 35 = 42.

questions.stem: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be the day after tomorrow?
questions.solution: Tomorrow is Thursday, and the day after that is Friday.

questions.stem: A film starts at 4:20 pm and lasts 1 hour and 35 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.solution: 4:20 plus 1 hour is 5:20, plus 35 minutes is 5:55 pm.

questions.stem: Sofia's holiday starts in 3 weeks and 4 days. How many days is that?
questions.solution: 3 weeks is 21 days, and 21 + 4 = 25 days.

questions.stem: Beads are threaded in a repeating pattern: red, blue, green, yellow, red, blue, green, yellow, and so on. What colour is the 10th bead?
questions.solution: The pattern repeats every 4 beads. Beads 9 and 10 begin the third round: red, then blue. So the 10th bead is blue.

questions.skill: days of the week plus days
questions.stem: Mina's birthday is on a Monday. Her party is 10 days after her birthday. On which day is the party?
questions.solution: 7 days after Monday is Monday again, and 3 more days make Thursday.

questions.stem: Pip counts down by 4 starting from 50: 50, 46, 42, and so on. What is the 6th number Pip says?
questions.solution: From the 1st to the 6th number there are 5 steps of 4, which is 20. So 50 - 20 = 30.

questions.stem: Buses leave a stop every 20 minutes. The first bus leaves at 8:00. At what time does the 5th bus leave?
questions.solution: Between the 1st and the 5th bus there are 4 gaps of 20 minutes, which is 80 minutes. 8:00 plus 80 minutes is 9:20.

questions.stem: A lesson starts at 9:45 and ends at 10:30. How many minutes does it last?
questions.solution: From 9:45 to 10:00 is 15 minutes and from 10:00 to 10:30 is 30 minutes. In all that is 45 minutes.

questions.stem: The numbers 1, 2, 3 are written over and over: 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, and so on. What is the sum of the first 7 numbers written?
questions.solution: The first seven numbers are 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1. Their sum is 6 + 6 + 1 = 13.

questions.stem: Today is Saturday. What day of the week was it 9 days ago?
questions.solution: 9 days is 1 week and 2 days. Two days before Saturday is Thursday.

solve.work: 9 days back = 2 days back; Saturday -> Thursday.

questions.stem: A row of 40 tiles repeats this pattern: white, white, grey, white, white, grey, and so on, starting with white. How many tiles in the row are grey?
questions.solution: Every third tile is grey: the 3rd, 6th, and so on. The last grey tile in 40 is the 39th, and 39 / 3 = 13.

solve.work: Grey at multiples of 3 up to 39: 13.

questions.stem: A frog hops back and forth between a pond and a log, which are 12 metres apart on a straight path. Each hop is exactly 4 metres. It starts at the pond, always hops towards the other end, and turns round at each end. How many metres from the pond is it after 7 hops?
questions.solution: The positions after each hop are 4, 8, 12, 8, 4, 0, 4. After the 7th hop the frog is 4 metres from the pond.

questions.stem: A row of numbers begins 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 5, 4, and goes on in the same way. What is the 10th number?
questions.solution: The rule is add 2, subtract 1, add 2, subtract 1, and so on. The row continues 6, 5, 7, so the 10th number is 7.

questions.stem: A plant is 5 cm tall on a Monday morning. It grows 2 cm every day. How many centimetres tall is it on the Monday morning two weeks later?
questions.solution: Two weeks is 14 days. The plant grows 14 times 2 = 28 cm, so it is 5 + 28 = 33 cm tall.

questions.stem: The day after tomorrow is Monday. What day was yesterday?
questions.solution: If the day after tomorrow is Monday, then tomorrow is Sunday and today is Saturday. Yesterday was Friday.

questions.stem: 24 lamps stand in a row and are numbered 1 to 24. Every 2nd lamp (2, 4, 6, and so on) has a red bulb. Every 3rd lamp (3, 6, 9, and so on) has a blue bulb. How many lamps have both a red and a blue bulb?
questions.solution: A lamp has both bulbs when its number is in both lists, so it is a multiple of 6: 6, 12, 18 and 24. That is 4 lamps.

questions.stem: In a certain month the 1st is a Friday. On which day of the week is the 23rd of that month?
questions.solution: From the 1st to the 23rd is 22 days, which is 3 weeks and 1 day. One day after Friday is Saturday.

questions.stem: An alarm rings every 45 minutes. The first ring is at 8:00. How many times does it ring from 8:00 up to and including 11:00?
questions.solution: The rings are at 8:00, 8:45, 9:30, 10:15 and 11:00. That is 5 rings.

questions.stem: The first row of a hall has 3 seats. Each next row has 2 more seats than the row before it. How many seats are in the first 5 rows altogether?
questions.solution: The rows have 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 seats. Their sum is 35.

questions.skill: days of the week: long jump
questions.stem: Today is Tuesday. What day of the week will it be 100 days from today?
questions.solution: 100 = 14 weeks and 2 days. Two days after Tuesday is Thursday.

questions.stem: A ball rolls back and forth along a straight track that is 6 metres long. It moves 1 metre every second, from the left end to the right end and back, without stopping, and it starts at the left end. How many metres from the left end is the ball after exactly 100 seconds?
questions.solution: One trip there and back takes 12 seconds, and 100 = 8 times 12 plus 4. After 96 seconds the ball is back at the left end, and 4 more seconds take it 4 metres along.

solve.work: Period 12 s; 100 mod 12 = 4, at 4 m going right.

questions.stem: 60 bulbs stand in a row, numbered 1 to 60. Every 3rd bulb (numbers 3, 6, 9, ...) is painted red. Every 4th bulb (numbers 4, 8, 12, ...) is painted blue, so some bulbs are both red and blue. How many bulbs are red but not blue?
questions.solution: There are 20 red bulbs (multiples of 3). Those that are also blue are multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, which is 5. So 20 - 5 = 15 are red but not blue.

solve.work: Multiples of 3 up to 60: 20; multiples of 12 (both): 5; red only = 20 - 5 = 15. Check: per block of 12, red-only are 3,6,9 -> 3 x 5 blocks = 15.

questions.stem: Today is Friday. Nina's holiday starts in 3 weeks and 4 days and lasts 10 days, counting both the first and the last day. On which day of the week is the last day of her holiday?
questions.solution: 3 weeks and 4 days is 25 days, so the first day is 4 days after Friday: Tuesday. The last day is 9 days after the first, and 9 days is 1 week and 2 days, so it is Thursday.

solve.work: Starts in 25 days: Friday + 4 = Tuesday; last day = start + 9 days -> Thursday.

questions.stem: The numbers are written in a row like this: one 1, then two 2s, then three 3s, then four 4s, and so on, each number written as many times as its value (1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, ...). What is the 20th number in the row?
questions.solution: The numbers up to 5 fill 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15 places. The 6s take places 16 to 21, so the 20th number is 6.

questions.stem: The numbers 4, 1, 7 are written over and over: 4, 1, 7, 4, 1, 7, and so on. What is the sum of the first 20 numbers written?
questions.solution: Each group of 3 adds to 12. Six groups use 18 numbers and give 72. The 19th and 20th numbers are 4 and 1, adding 5, so the total is 77.

questions.stem: Squares are made from matchsticks. One square uses 4 matchsticks. Two squares side by side, sharing one stick, use 7 matchsticks. Three squares in a row use 10 matchsticks. How many matchsticks do 10 squares in a row use?
questions.solution: Each extra square adds 3 matchsticks. From 1 square to 10 squares there are 9 additions, so 4 + 27 = 31.

questions.stem: Two buses leave the depot together at 8:00. One bus is back at the depot every 12 minutes, the other every 18 minutes. At what time are both buses at the depot together again for the first time?
questions.solution: The first bus is at the depot at multiples of 12 minutes and the other at multiples of 18. The first number in both lists is 36, so they meet again at 8:36.

questions.stem: Rosa starts a book on a Monday. She reads 4 pages on each day from Monday to Friday and 10 pages on each Saturday and Sunday. On which day does her total first reach 100 pages or more?
questions.solution: One week gives 5 times 4 + 2 times 10 = 40 pages. After 2 weeks she has 80. In the third week she has 84, 88, 92, 96 and then 100 after Friday.

solve.work: 40 pages a week; after 2 weeks 80, then Mon 84, Tue 88, Wed 92, Thu 96, Fri 100.

questions.stem: A lift starts at floor 1 and goes up to floor 9, stopping once at every floor on the way. Then it comes down to floor 1, again stopping once at every floor, and goes straight back up in the same way, all day. Each time it reaches floor 1 or floor 9 counts as one stop. Its 1st stop is at floor 1. At which floor is its 30th stop?
questions.solution: One full cycle (floor 1 up to 9, then down to 2) has 16 stops, and stop 17 is floor 1 again. Stop 30 is the same as stop 14: floors 1 to 9 are stops 1 to 9, then 8, 7, 6, 5, 4 are stops 10 to 14. So it is floor 4.

solve.work: Stops cycle with period 16: 1..9 (stops 1-9), 8..2 (stops 10-16). Stop 30: (30-1) mod 16 = 13 -> 5th of 8,7,6,5,4 = floor 4. Direct list: stops 26-30 are 8,7,6,5,4.

questions.stem: Anna is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Chen. Dara is shorter than Chen. Who is the second tallest of the four children?
questions.solution: The clues give the order Anna, Ben, Chen, Dara from tallest to shortest. The second tallest is Ben.

solve.work: Anna > Ben > Chen > Dara; second tallest is Ben.

questions.stem: Nia is 3rd from the front of a queue and 6th from the back of the same queue. How many children are in the queue?
questions.solution: Nia is counted in both numbers. There are 2 children in front of her and 5 behind her, plus Nia herself: 2 + 5 + 1 = 8.

questions.stem: Ola, Pia, Raj and Sue each have one pet, and the pets are a cat, a dog, a fish and a bird, all different. Ola's pet has no fur and cannot fly. Sue's pet has wings. Raj is afraid of dogs, so his pet is not the dog. Who has the cat?
questions.solution: The fish has no fur and cannot fly, so Ola has the fish. The bird has wings, so Sue has the bird. Raj and Pia are left with the cat and the dog, and Raj has no dog, so Raj has the cat.

solve.work: Ola: no fur, no wings -> fish; Sue -> bird; Raj not dog -> cat; Pia dog.

questions.stem: Four kangaroos sit in a row on a bench: Zoe, Yan, Xena and Walt. Zoe sits at one end of the bench. Yan sits next to Zoe. Xena sits between Yan and Walt. Who sits at the other end of the bench?
questions.solution: Zoe is at one end and Yan is next to her. Xena is between Yan and Walt, so the row is Zoe, Yan, Xena, Walt. The other end is Walt.

solve.work: Order Zoe, Yan, Xena, Walt; Walt at the other end.

questions.stem: Ari, Bea and Cy each say one thing about today. Ari: "It is raining." Bea: "It is not raining." Cy: "It is a cold day." Exactly one of the three children is lying. Who must be telling the truth?
questions.solution: Ari and Bea say opposite things, so exactly one of them is lying. Only one child lies in all, so Cy must be telling the truth. We cannot tell which of Ari and Bea is the truthful one.

solve.work: Ari and Bea contradict, so the one liar is one of them; Cy tells the truth.

questions.stem: A 3 by 3 table is filled with the numbers 1, 2 and 3 so that every row and every column has each of the numbers exactly once. Row 1 is: 1, _, _. Row 2 is: _, 1, 2. Row 3 is empty. What number goes in row 3, column 1 (bottom left)?
questions.solution: Row 2 has 1 and 2, so its first number is 3. Column 1 now has 1 and 3, so the bottom-left number is 2.

solve.work: Row 2 col 1 = 3; column 1 has 1, 3 so row 3 col 1 = 2 (grid fully determined: 1 2 3 / 3 1 2 / 2 3 1).

questions.stem: In Class 3B, every child who has a dog also has a cat. Kim is a child in Class 3B and Kim has a dog. Which sentence must be true?
questions.solution: The rule says anyone with a dog also has a cat. Kim has a dog, so Kim has a cat. Nothing is said about birds or about how many dogs Kim has.

solve.work: Dog implies cat; Kim has a dog, so Kim has a cat.

questions.stem: Eli finished 4th in a race with 9 runners. Fay's place number was 3 bigger than Eli's. There were no ties. How many runners finished behind Fay?
questions.solution: Fay finished in 4 + 3 = 7th place. The runners behind her are in places 8 and 9, which is 9 - 7 = 2 runners.

questions.stem: Mina thinks of a number between 20 and 30. The number is even. Its digits add up to 8. What is Mina's number?
questions.solution: The even numbers between 20 and 30 are 22, 24, 26 and 28, with digit sums 4, 6, 8 and 10. Only 26 has digit sum 8.

solve.work: Even numbers 22..28 with digit sum 8: only 26.

questions.stem: Jo scored more points than Kit. Kit and Lu scored the same number of points. Mo scored fewer points than Lu. Which sentence must be true?
choices: Mo scored the same as Kit.
questions.solution: Putting the clues together: Jo is above Kit, Kit equals Lu, and Lu is above Mo. So Jo is above Mo. The other three sentences all go against the clues.

solve.work: Jo > Kit = Lu > Mo, so Jo > Mo; the other three are false.

questions.stem: A 4 by 4 table is filled with the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 so that every row and every column has each number exactly once. Row 1: 1, _, _, 4. Row 2: _, 4, _, _. Row 3: _, _, 1, _. Row 4: 2, _, _, _. What number is in the bottom right square (row 4, column 4)?
questions.solution: Column 1 has 1 and 2, and row 2 has a 4, so row 2 starts with 3 and row 3 starts with 4. Row 2 then needs 1 and 2 in its last two places, and column 3 already has a 1, so row 2 is 3, 4, 2, 1. Now row 1 needs 3 in column 3, so it is 1, 2, 3, 4. Row 3 has 4, _, 1, _ with 2 and 3 left; column 2 has 2 and 4, so row 3 is 4, 3, 1, 2. Row 4 is 2, 1, 4, 3, and the bottom right is 3.

solve.work: Col 1 forces r2c1=3, r3c1=4; r1=1,3,2,4 leads to contradiction in col 3, so r1=1,2,3,4 and the grid ends 2,1,4,3; bottom right 3.

questions.stem: Someone broke a vase, and it was one of Asha, Bruno, Chi and Dev. They say: Asha: "Bruno did it." Bruno: "Chi did it." Chi: "Bruno is lying." Dev: "I did not do it." Exactly one of the four children is lying. Who broke the vase?
questions.solution: Try each suspect. If Asha did it, Asha and Bruno both lie. If Chi did it, Asha and Chi both lie. If Dev did it, Asha, Bruno and Dev all lie. If Bruno did it, only Bruno lies (Asha, Chi and Dev are right). So Bruno did it.

solve.work: Bruno and Chi contradict, so Asha and Dev are truthful: Bruno did it (Bruno lies, Chi true).

questions.stem: Ana, Ben, Cy and Dev sit in four seats in a row, numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4 from the left. Ana does not sit at either end. Ben sits next to Ana. Cy sits in a higher-numbered seat than Ana. Dev does not sit at either end. Who sits in seat 1?
questions.solution: Ana and Dev are not at the ends, so they take seats 2 and 3. If Ana were in seat 3, Cy would need seat 4, Dev would have seat 2, and Ben would be left with seat 1, which is not next to Ana. So Ana is in seat 2 and Dev in seat 3. Cy is higher than Ana, so Cy is in seat 4, and Ben is in seat 1.

solve.work: Ana and Dev take seats 2, 3; Ana in 3 leaves no seat for Ben; so Ana 2, Dev 3, Cy 4, Ben 1.

questions.stem: Five children are Hugo, Ida, Jin, Kara and Leo. Hugo is shorter than Kara. Jin is shorter than Ida. Ida is shorter than Hugo. Leo is shorter than Jin. All five have different heights. How many of the children are shorter than Hugo?
questions.solution: Put the clues in order from tallest: Kara, then Hugo, then Ida, then Jin, then Leo. The children shorter than Hugo are Ida, Jin and Leo, which is 3.

solve.work: Leo < Jin < Ida < Hugo < Kara: 3 shorter than Hugo.

questions.stem: In a queue, Tom has 4 children in front of him. Una is behind Tom, with 3 children between Tom and Una. There are 2 children behind Una. How many children are in the queue?
questions.solution: Count from the front: 4 children, Tom, 3 children, Una, and 2 children. That is 4 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 11.

questions.skill: statements about the number of liars
questions.stem: Four kangaroos make statements. Kia: "Exactly one of us four is lying." Bo: "Exactly two of us four are lying." Cal: "Exactly three of us four are lying." Dee: "All four of us are lying." Each kangaroo either always tells the truth or always lies. Who tells the truth?
questions.solution: At most one statement can be true, since they give different numbers of liars. If nobody were truthful, all four would be lying and Dee would be right, which is a contradiction. So exactly one is truthful and three are lying, so the truthful one is the one who said three: Cal.

solve.work: At most one statement can be true; none true makes Dee true, so exactly one true means 3 liars: Cal.

questions.stem: Four boxes are numbered 1 to 4 and a prize is in one of them. The labels say: Box 1: "The prize is in this box." Box 2: "The prize is not in this box." Box 3: "The prize is in box 1 or box 2." Box 4: "The prize is not in box 3." Exactly one label is true. Where is the prize?
questions.solution: Test each place. Prize in box 1: labels 1 and 2 are true. Prize in box 2: labels 3 and 4 are true. Prize in box 4: labels 2 and 4 are true. Prize in box 3: only label 2 is true. So the prize is in box 3.

solve.work: Count true labels for prize in 1..4: 2, 2, 1, 2; only box 3 gives exactly one.

questions.stem: A drawer holds 6 red socks, 6 blue socks and 6 black socks, all mixed up. Mo takes socks out in the dark, one at a time. How many socks must he take to be sure that two of them are the same colour?
questions.solution: In the worst case the first three socks are all different colours: one red, one blue and one black. The 4th sock must match one of them. So Mo must take 4 socks.

solve.work: Three colours: 3 socks could all differ, the 4th forces a pair.

questions.stem: Eve, Finn, Gia and Hal each play a different instrument: piano, drums, flute or violin. Eve and Finn do not play the piano or the drums. Eve does not play the flute. Hal does not play the drums. Who plays the drums?
questions.solution: Eve and Finn play the flute and the violin, in some order, and Eve does not play the flute, so Eve has the violin and Finn the flute. Gia and Hal share the piano and the drums, and Hal does not play the drums, so Gia plays the drums.

solve.work: Eve violin; Finn flute; Hal piano (not drums); Gia drums.

questions.stem: Four teams play each other exactly once, 6 matches in all, and there are no draws. Team A won 3 matches, team B won 1 match and team C won 1 match. How many matches did team D win?
questions.solution: Each match has exactly one winner, so the teams won 6 matches in total. A, B and C won 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 of them, so D won 6 - 5 = 1 match.

solve.work: 6 wins in total, 6 - 5 = 1; realisable with A beating all and B, C, D in a cycle.

questions.stem: A 4 by 4 table is filled with the letters A, B, C and D so that every row and every column has each letter exactly once. Row 1: B, _, D, _. Row 2: _, _, B, _. Row 3: all empty. Row 4: _, _, _, A. Which letter is in row 3, column 2?
questions.solution: Column 4 already has an A at the bottom, so in row 1 the last place is C and the second place is A. Row 2 then needs D in its last place (column 4 has C and A, and B is used), so row 2 is A, C, B, D (its last two letters A and C go in columns 1 and 2, and column 2 already has A). In column 3 the letters D and B are used, so row 4 has C and row 3 has A there, and column 4 gives B for row 3. Row 3 has C and D left for columns 1 and 2, and column 2 already has C, so the letter in row 3, column 2 is D.

solve.work: r1 = B A D C, r2 = A C B D, col 4 gives r3c4 = B, so r3c2 in {B,D} minus B = D (r3 = C D A B).

questions.stem: The last slice of a cake was taken by one of Mel, Ned, Oli, Pat and Quin. They said: Mel: "It was Ned or Oli." Ned: "It was not me." Oli: "It was Pat." Pat: "It was Mel." Quin: "Ned is lying." Exactly one of the five statements is true. Who took the slice?
questions.solution: Test each person. If Mel took it, Ned and Pat are both right. If Ned took it, Mel and Quin are both right. If Oli took it, Mel and Ned are both right. If Pat took it, Ned and Oli are both right. If Quin took it, Ned is right and Quin is wrong, and the other three are wrong, so exactly one statement is true: Quin.

solve.work: Ned and Quin are complementary so exactly one of them is true; Mel, Oli, Pat false rules out Ned, Oli, Pat, Mel: Quin.

questions.stem: Lia, Max and Noor each have one pet (a cat, a dog or a rabbit) and each plays one sport (tennis, judo or soccer), all different. Lia's pet is not a cat or a dog. Noor's pet is not a dog. The cat's owner plays tennis. The rabbit's owner plays judo. Which sentence is true?
choices: Max has the dog and plays soccer.
Lia has the cat and plays judo.
Noor has the rabbit and plays tennis.
Lia has the rabbit and plays tennis.
questions.answer: Max has the dog and plays soccer.
questions.solution: Lia has the rabbit. Noor does not have the dog or the rabbit, so Noor has the cat and Max has the dog. The cat's owner Noor plays tennis, and the rabbit's owner Lia plays judo, so Max plays soccer.

solve.answer: Max has the dog and plays soccer.
solve.work: Lia rabbit (judo), Noor cat (tennis), Max dog (soccer).

questions.skill: truth-tellers and liars in a circle
questions.stem: Six kangaroos stand in a circle. Each one is either a truth-teller who always tells the truth, or a liar who always lies. Each kangaroo says: "The kangaroo next to me, going clockwise, is a liar." How many of the six kangaroos are liars?
questions.solution: A truth-teller's clockwise neighbour must be a liar. A liar says something false, so their clockwise neighbour is a truth-teller. So truth-tellers and liars alternate all the way round, and 3 of the 6 are liars.

solve.work: Truth-teller is followed by a liar and a liar by a truth-teller: alternating, 3 liars.

questions.stem: Eight boxes stand in a row. Some boxes hold a coin. Each box has a label that says how many coins are in the boxes right next to it (the box on its left and the box on its right, where they exist). A box with a coin has a label too. From left to right the labels are 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1. How many coins are there altogether?
questions.solution: Box 1 has only one neighbour, so box 2 holds a coin; likewise box 8 shows 1, so box 7 holds a coin. Box 3 shows 2, so boxes 2 and 4 hold coins. Box 5 shows 2, so boxes 4 and 6 hold coins. Box 6 shows 1 and box 7 holds a coin, so box 5 is empty. Box 4 shows 1 and box 5 is empty, so box 3 holds a coin. Box 2 shows 1, so box 1 is empty, and box 7 shows 1 with box 6 full, so box 8 is empty. The coins are in boxes 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7: 5 coins.

solve.work: Solving c2=1, c4=1, c6=1, c7=1, c8=0, c5=0, c3=1, c1=0: coins 0,1,1,1,0,1,1,0 = 5; all labels check.

questions.skill: order of a race from clues
questions.stem: Ana, Bo, Cy, Dee and Eli ran a race with no ties. Ana finished before Bo and before Cy. Eli was not last. Bo finished somewhere between Dee and Eli. Dee finished somewhere between Ana and Eli. Who finished 4th?
questions.solution: Dee is between Ana and Eli, so the order of those three is Ana, Dee, Eli or Eli, Dee, Ana. The second would put Bo (between Dee and Eli) ahead of Ana, but Ana is before Bo. So it is Ana, Dee, Eli, and Bo comes between Dee and Eli: Ana, Dee, Bo, Eli. Cy is behind Ana, and Eli is not last, so Cy is last. The order is Ana, Dee, Bo, Eli, Cy, so Eli is 4th.

solve.work: Ana<Dee<Bo<Eli (the reverse case contradicts Ana before Bo); Eli not last so Cy is 5th; Eli 4th.

questions.skill: worst case for three of a kind
questions.stem: A bag holds 5 red balls, 5 green balls and 5 blue balls. Pia takes balls out without looking, one at a time. How many balls must she take to be sure that she has three balls of the same colour?
questions.solution: In the worst case she has 2 balls of each colour, which is 6 balls and no colour three times. The 7th ball must make three of one colour. So she must take 7 balls.

solve.work: Worst case 2 of each colour (6), the 7th makes three of one colour.

questions.stem: Three different whole numbers, each at least 1, add up to 9. Which sentence must be true?
choices: At least one of them is odd.
At least one of them is even.
questions.answer: At least one of them is odd.
questions.solution: List all the triples: 1, 2, 6 and 1, 3, 5 and 2, 3, 4. Each triple has an odd number, so the first sentence is always true. The triple 1, 3, 5 has no even number, 2, 3, 4 has no 1, and 1, 2, 6 has largest number 6, so the others can fail.

solve.answer: At least one of them is odd.
solve.work: Sets {1,2,6},{1,3,5},{2,3,4}; an odd sum needs an odd number; {1,3,5} has no even, {2,3,4} no 1, largest not always 5.

questions.stem: Ravi, Sana and Tao each say one thing about today. Ravi: "Today is Tuesday or Wednesday." Sana: "Tomorrow is Thursday." Tao: "Today is a day from Monday to Friday." Exactly two of the three are right. What day is it today?
questions.solution: Check each day. Monday: only Tao is right. Tuesday: Ravi and Tao are right, Sana is not. Wednesday: all three are right. Thursday: only Tao is right. So it is Tuesday.

solve.work: Sana means Wednesday; Wednesday makes 3 right, Tuesday 2, other weekdays 1.

questions.stem: Sam wants to fry 3 pancakes. His pan holds 2 pancakes at a time. A pancake must be fried on each of its two sides, and each side needs 2 minutes. Sam can take a pancake out and put it back later. What is the shortest time, in minutes, in which all 3 pancakes can be done?
questions.solution: There are 3 x 2 = 6 sides to fry, and the pan fries 2 sides at a time, so at least 3 rounds are needed, each of 2 minutes. That is 6 minutes. It works: round 1 fries one side of pancakes 1 and 2, round 2 the other side of pancake 1 and one side of pancake 3, round 3 the other sides of pancakes 2 and 3.

solve.work: 6 sides, 2 at a time, 2 min per round: 3 rounds = 6 min (rotate A1B1, A2C1, B2C2).

questions.stem: Ali, Bea and Cam stand in a line to buy tickets. In how many different orders can the three of them stand in the line?
questions.solution: Any of the 3 can be first. Then 2 are left for second place, and the last child is third. That gives 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 orders.

questions.stem: Kofi has 3 shirts and 5 pairs of trousers. Each day he wears one shirt with one pair of trousers. How many different outfits can he make?
questions.solution: Each of the 3 shirts can go with each of the 5 pairs of trousers, so there are 3 x 5 = 15 outfits.

questions.stem: Five friends meet. Every friend shakes hands exactly once with each of the other four friends. How many handshakes are there in total?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 friends shakes 4 hands, which counts 5 x 4 = 20, but every handshake is counted by both people. So there are 20 / 2 = 10 handshakes.

questions.skill: pairs where order does not matter
questions.stem: An ice cream shop has 4 flavours: vanilla, mango, kiwi and lemon. Dina wants a bowl with 2 different flavours. A bowl of vanilla and mango is the same as a bowl of mango and vanilla. How many different bowls can she choose?
questions.solution: List them: vanilla with each of the other 3 (3 bowls), then mango with kiwi and lemon (2 bowls), then kiwi with lemon (1 bowl). That is 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 bowls.

questions.stem: Mia wants to pay exactly 7 cents. She has plenty of 1-cent coins and 2-cent coins. The order of the coins does not matter, only how many of each she uses. In how many different ways can she pay?
questions.solution: She can use 0, 1, 2 or 3 two-cent coins, and the rest in one-cent coins: 7, 5 (with 1 two), 3 (with 2 twos), 1 (with 3 twos). Four ways in all, since 4 two-cent coins would be 8 cents.

questions.stem: A red die and a blue die are rolled together. The two numbers that land face up add up to 4. In how many different ways can this happen? (Red 1 with blue 3 is different from red 3 with blue 1.)
questions.solution: List the red number first: 1 and 3, 2 and 2, 3 and 1. There are 3 ways.

questions.stem: How many different 3-digit numbers can be written using only the digits 1 and 2? A digit may be used more than once.
questions.solution: Each of the 3 places can be 1 or 2, so there are 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 numbers: 111, 112, 121, 122, 211, 212, 221, 222.

questions.stem: A club has 4 children. They choose one leader and one helper, and the leader and the helper must be different children. In how many ways can they choose?
questions.solution: There are 4 choices for the leader. Then 3 children are left for the helper. So there are 4 x 3 = 12 ways.

questions.stem: A coin is tossed 4 times and the result of each toss, heads or tails, is written down in order. In how many of the possible results is there exactly one head?
questions.solution: The single head can come on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th toss, and all other tosses are tails. That is 4 results.

solve.work: The head can be in any of 4 positions.

questions.stem: Ali, Bea and Cam sit on a bench with 3 seats in a row. Ali always sits in the middle seat. In how many different ways can the three of them sit?
questions.solution: Ali is in the middle. Bea can take the left or the right seat, and Cam takes the other one. So there are 2 ways.

solve.work: Bea and Cam fill the two end seats in 2 ways.

questions.stem: A secret code is 3 different letters chosen from A, B, C and D and written in a row. How many different codes are there?
questions.solution: There are 4 choices for the first letter, 3 for the second and 2 for the third. So there are 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 codes.

questions.stem: Four friends, Ada, Bo, Cy and Dee, stand in a line. Ada and Bo must stand next to each other. How many different orders are possible?
questions.solution: Treat Ada and Bo as one block. The block and the other two children can be ordered in 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 ways. Inside the block Ada and Bo can swap, so there are 6 x 2 = 12 orders.

questions.stem: Mina has three discs: one red, one blue and one green. She builds a tower from some or all of the discs, using each disc at most once. The tower is at least 1 disc high, and the order of the discs from bottom to top matters. How many different towers can she build?
questions.solution: A tower of 1 disc: 3 ways. A tower of 2 discs: 3 x 2 = 6 ways. A tower of 3 discs: 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 ways. In all 3 + 6 + 6 = 15 towers.

questions.stem: A flag has 3 stripes, one above the other. Each stripe is red, white or blue. Two stripes that touch must have different colours, but the top and bottom stripes may have the same colour. How many different flags are there?
questions.solution: The top stripe can have 3 colours. The middle stripe must differ from it: 2 colours. The bottom stripe must differ from the middle one: 2 colours. So there are 3 x 2 x 2 = 12 flags.

questions.skill: numbers from digits, no leading zero
questions.stem: Using each of the digits 0, 1 and 2 exactly once, how many different 3-digit numbers can be written? A number may not start with 0.
questions.solution: The first digit is 1 or 2. If it is 1, the other two digits give 102 and 120. If it is 2, they give 201 and 210. That is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: A strip of 4 squares in a row is covered exactly by tiles. Each tile covers either 1 square or 2 squares that are next to each other. Tiles do not overlap. In how many ways can the strip be covered?
questions.solution: Write the tile sizes from left to right: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2. There are 5 ways.

questions.stem: Choose two different numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. The order of the two numbers does not matter. In how many ways can you choose them so that their sum is even?
questions.solution: A sum is even only when both numbers are even or both are odd. There are 4 even numbers, giving 6 pairs, and 4 odd numbers, giving 6 pairs. So 6 + 6 = 12 pairs.

solve.work: Both even C(4,2)=6 plus both odd 6 = 12.

questions.stem: A pizza shop offers 4 extra toppings: ham, olives, peppers and corn. Jo may choose any of them or none at all, and each topping is used at most once. How many different pizzas can Jo order?
questions.solution: For each topping Jo says yes or no: 2 choices each. So there are 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16 pizzas, and one of them has no extra topping.

solve.work: Each topping in or out: 2^4 = 16 (including plain).

questions.stem: A square is cut into 4 small squares, 2 rows of 2. Each small square is painted red or blue, and exactly 2 of them are red. The big square is never turned: two paintings with the red squares in different places count as different. How many paintings are there?
questions.solution: Choose the two red squares among the four. With the squares called 1 to 4, the pairs are 12, 13, 14, 23, 24 and 34. That is 6 paintings.

questions.stem: A set of dominoes has one tile for every pair of numbers from 0 to 3. A tile may have the same number on both halves, like 2 and 2. The tile with 1 and 3 is the same as the tile with 3 and 1. How many tiles are in the set?
questions.solution: Tiles with equal halves: 0-0, 1-1, 2-2, 3-3, which is 4 tiles. Tiles with different halves: 4 x 3 / 2 = 6 tiles. In all 4 + 6 = 10 tiles.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have digits that add up to 4? (A 3-digit number does not start with 0.)
questions.solution: List by the first digit. First digit 1: 103, 112, 121, 130. First digit 2: 202, 211, 220. First digit 3: 301, 310. First digit 4: 400. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 numbers.

questions.stem: Four children, Ana, Ben, Cal and Dee, stand in a line. Ana may not be first and Ben may not be last. How many different orders are possible?
questions.solution: There are 24 orders in all. Ana first: 6 orders. Ben last: 6 orders. Both Ana first and Ben last: 2 orders, which were taken off twice. So 24 - 6 - 6 + 2 = 14.

questions.stem: Lena climbs a staircase of 6 steps. Each move she goes up either 1 step or 2 steps. In how many different ways can she reach the top, going up exactly 6 steps in total?
questions.solution: Let the number of ways to reach step n be W(n). To land on step n, her last move came from step n-1 or n-2, so W(n) = W(n-1) + W(n-2). W(1)=1, W(2)=2, W(3)=3, W(4)=5, W(5)=8, W(6)=13.

questions.stem: Tom stacks 5 discs in a tower: 3 identical red discs and 2 identical blue discs. Two towers look the same if the colours are in the same places from bottom to top. How many different-looking towers can he build?
questions.solution: Only the places of the 2 blue discs matter. Choose 2 of the 5 places: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 ways.

questions.stem: Four countries A, B, C and D are painted. A touches B, C and D. C touches A, B and D. B touches A and C only, and D touches A and C only (B and D do not touch). Each country is painted red, green or blue, and countries that touch must have different colours. How many different paintings are there?
questions.solution: A has 3 colour choices, and C must differ from A: 2 choices. B touches both A and C, so only the third colour is left for B. D also touches both A and C, so D gets that same third colour. Total 3 x 2 = 6.

solve.work: A 3 ways, C 2, then B and D each forced to the third colour: 6.

questions.stem: Seven identical sweets are shared among three children, Ana, Bo and Cy. Every child gets at least one sweet, and all 7 sweets are given out. In how many different ways can the sweets be shared?
questions.solution: The shares, as a set, can be 5,1,1 or 4,2,1 or 3,3,1 or 3,2,2. Shares 5,1,1 can be given out in 3 ways, 4,2,1 in 6 ways, 3,3,1 in 3 ways and 3,2,2 in 3 ways. So 3 + 6 + 3 + 3 = 15.

solve.work: Give each one, share 4 among 3: C(6,2) = 15.

questions.stem: A big rectangle is made of 2 rows and 3 columns of equal small squares, 6 squares in all. How many rectangles can be found whose sides run along the grid lines? Count the small squares, the big rectangle itself and everything in between.
questions.solution: A rectangle is fixed by choosing 2 of the 3 horizontal lines (3 ways) and 2 of the 4 vertical lines (6 ways). That gives 3 x 6 = 18 rectangles.

solve.work: C(3,2) row-line pairs x C(4,2) column-line pairs = 3 x 6 = 18.

questions.stem: Kai has four coins worth 1, 2, 3 and 5 cents. He picks one or more of them and adds up their values. How many different totals can he get?
questions.solution: There are 15 ways to pick coins, but some give the same total (for example 3, and 1+2). The totals are 1 to 11, and each can be made: 1, 2, 3, 4=1+3, 5, 6=1+5, 7=2+5, 8=3+5, 9=1+3+5, 10=2+3+5, 11=1+2+3+5. So 11 different totals.

solve.work: Subset sums of {1,2,3,5} cover every total 1 to 11: 11.

questions.stem: Two identical counters are put on two different squares of a 3 by 3 board. They must not be on squares that share a side (squares touching only at a corner are allowed). In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: Two squares out of 9 can be chosen in 9 x 8 / 2 = 36 ways. Pairs of squares that share a side: 6 across rows and 6 down columns make 12. So 36 - 12 = 24.

questions.stem: Four children, numbered 1 to 4, each took off a coat, and the coats, also numbered 1 to 4, were mixed up. Each child is given one coat back. In how many ways can the coats be given back so that nobody gets their own coat?
questions.solution: Child 1 can get coat 2, 3 or 4. Say child 1 gets coat 2. Then either child 2 gets coat 1 (and children 3 and 4 swap coats: 1 way), or child 2 gets coat 3 or 4 and the remaining coats go round in exactly 1 way each: that is 3 ways for child 1 getting coat 2. So 3 x 3 = 9 ways.

questions.stem: A rectangle is longer than it is wide, so it is not a square. How many mirror lines (lines of symmetry) does it have?
questions.solution: One mirror line joins the midpoints of the two long sides and one joins the midpoints of the two short sides. The diagonals are not mirror lines because the sides are unequal. So there are 2.

solve.work: Non-square rectangle: only the two lines through midpoints of opposite sides.

questions.stem: Mia stands facing north. She makes a quarter turn clockwise (towards her right) and then a half turn (she turns right around). Which way does she face now?
questions.solution: A quarter turn clockwise from north leaves her facing east. A half turn then makes her face the opposite way, which is west.

solve.work: N -> quarter clockwise E -> half turn W.

questions.stem: A paper strip has 8 squares in a row, numbered 1 to 8 from left to right. It is folded in half so that square 8 lands on square 1. Which numbered square lands on square 3?
questions.solution: The folded squares meet in pairs: 1 with 8, 2 with 7, 3 with 6 and 4 with 5. Each pair adds to 9, so square 3 meets square 6.

questions.skill: counting triangles in a split triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has one straight line drawn from its top corner to a point on the opposite side. The line cuts the triangle into two smaller triangles. How many triangles can you find in all, counting the whole triangle too?
questions.solution: There are the two small triangles and the whole triangle, which makes 3.

solve.work: Two small triangles plus the whole one.

questions.stem: Leo stands on a square of a big grid. One move takes him one square right, left, up or down. He moves 4 squares right, 3 up, 2 left and 3 down. How many squares to the right of his starting square is he now?
questions.solution: Up and down cancel: 3 up and 3 down. Sideways he goes 4 right and 2 left, which leaves him 4 - 2 = 2 squares to the right.

solve.work: 4 right - 2 left = 2; ups and downs cancel.

questions.skill: vertical mirror line of a letter
questions.stem: Which of these capital letters, written in plain block shape, has a vertical mirror line, so that its left half is the mirror image of its right half?
questions.solution: M can be folded down its middle so that the two halves match. F, G and R look different on the left and on the right.

solve.work: M is left-right symmetric; G, F, R are not.

questions.stem: A rectangular sheet is folded in half once. A hole is punched through both layers, well away from the fold and from the edges. The sheet is opened out again. How many holes does it have?
questions.solution: The punch goes through two layers, so it makes one hole in each half of the sheet. That makes 2 holes.

solve.work: One punch through two layers gives two holes.

questions.stem: Three equal squares are joined edge to edge to make an L shape: two squares side by side, and a third square on top of the left one. How many straight sides does the outline of this L shape have?
questions.solution: Walking round the outline we go along the bottom, up the right side of the lower row, left along the top of the right square, up the right side of the upper square, left along the top and down the left side. That is 6 sides.

questions.stem: The hour hand of a clock points at the 12. It makes a half turn clockwise and then a quarter turn anticlockwise (the other way). At which number does it point now?
questions.solution: A half turn clockwise takes it from 12 to 6. A quarter turn back the other way moves it 3 numbers, from 6 to 3.

questions.stem: How many mirror lines does a square have?
questions.solution: A square has 2 mirror lines through the midpoints of opposite sides and 2 along its diagonals. That is 4.

questions.stem: A robot stands in the bottom-left square of a board with 5 columns and 5 rows. Columns are numbered 1 to 5 from the left and rows 1 to 5 from the bottom, so the robot starts in column 1, row 1. One step takes it one square. It makes 3 steps right, 2 steps up, 1 step left, 2 steps up and 2 steps right. In which square does it stop?
questions.solution: Sideways: 1 + 3 - 1 + 2 = column 5. Upwards: 1 + 2 + 2 = row 5. The robot stays on the board all the way, so it stops in column 5, row 5.

questions.skill: mirror lines of a plus shape
questions.stem: Five equal squares are joined to make a plus sign: one square in the middle and one square joined to each of its four sides. How many mirror lines does this plus shape have?
questions.solution: The plus can be folded along the vertical line through its middle, along the horizontal line through its middle, and along each of the two diagonals through the middle square. That is 4 mirror lines.

solve.work: Vertical, horizontal and both diagonals through the centre square.

questions.stem: A long strip of paper is folded in half, and then folded in half again in the same direction, so it has 4 layers. One straight cut is made all the way across the folded strip, from one long edge to the other, away from the folds. The strip is opened out. Into how many separate pieces has it been cut?
questions.solution: The cut goes through 4 layers, so the opened strip has 4 cuts across it. Four cuts in a strip make 5 pieces.

solve.work: Cut at x in the folded strip hits the strip at x, L/2-x, L/2+x, L-x: 4 cuts, 5 pieces.

questions.skill: path on a grid, way back
questions.stem: An ant starts at a corner of a grid and walks along the grid lines. Each move is one square length. It walks 3 moves right, 4 moves up, 1 move left, 2 moves down and 1 move left. What is the smallest number of moves it needs to get back to its starting corner, still moving along grid lines?
questions.solution: Sideways it has gone 3 - 1 - 1 = 1 to the right. Upwards it has gone 4 - 2 = 2. To get back it needs 1 move left and 2 moves down, which is 3 moves.

questions.stem: A strip is made of 4 equal squares in a row. How many rectangles can you find in it, counting single squares and the whole strip? (A square is also a rectangle.)
questions.solution: There are 4 rectangles of one square, 3 of two squares, 2 of three squares and 1 of four squares. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

questions.stem: A square piece of paper has each of its four corners cut off by a straight cut joining the midpoints of the two sides that meet at that corner. What shape is the piece left in the middle?
choices: a rectangle that is not a square
questions.solution: The cuts join the midpoints of neighbouring sides, so the four cuts meet at the four midpoints. The piece left has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, so it is a smaller square.

solve.work: Joining the four midpoints gives a square turned 45 degrees.

questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock makes one full turn in an hour. How many quarter turns does it make from 3:00 to 4:30?
questions.solution: From 3:00 to 4:30 is 90 minutes. A quarter turn takes 15 minutes, so the hand makes 90 / 15 = 6 quarter turns.

questions.stem: A robot faces north. It obeys commands in order. R means a quarter turn to the right, L a quarter turn to the left and U a half turn (turn around). The commands are R, R, U, L, R, L, U, R. Which way does it face at the end?
questions.solution: Follow it step by step: R gives east, R gives south, U gives north, L gives west, R gives north, L gives west, U gives east, R gives south.

solve.work: Quarter-turn count +1+1+2-1+1-1+2+1=6, 6 mod 4=2: South; checked step by step.

questions.skill: mirror lines of a shaded pattern
questions.stem: A square is divided into four equal small squares, two rows of two. The top-left and the bottom-right small squares are shaded and the other two are not. How many mirror lines does this pattern have? (A mirror line must send shaded squares onto shaded squares.)
questions.solution: The two diagonals of the big square work: along one the shaded squares stay put and along the other they swap places. The vertical and horizontal middle lines would send a shaded square onto an unshaded one. So there are 2.

solve.work: Both diagonals work (each keeps the shaded pair shaded); midlines swap shaded with unshaded.

questions.stem: A square card has letters at its corners: A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right and D at the bottom-left. The card lies flat and is turned a quarter turn clockwise, and then a further half turn clockwise. Which letter is now at the bottom-right corner?
questions.solution: Altogether the card is turned three quarter turns clockwise. Each quarter turn moves a letter one corner clockwise, so after three the letter at the bottom-right is the one that started one corner clockwise before it, at the bottom-left. That is D.

solve.work: 3/4 turn clockwise = quarter anticlockwise; bottom-left D moves to bottom-right.

questions.stem: A big square is made of 9 equal small squares, 3 rows of 3. How many squares of any size can you find, if every side of a square must lie along the lines between small squares?
questions.solution: There are 9 small squares, 4 squares made of 2 by 2 small squares and 1 big square. That is 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.

questions.stem: A strip of paper has 12 squares in a row, numbered 1 to 12 from left to right. It is folded in half so that square 12 lands on square 1. The folded strip is then folded in half again so that square 6 lands on square 1. A hole is punched through all the layers where square 2 lies. The strip is opened out. What is the sum of the numbers of the squares that have a hole?
questions.solution: After the first fold square 11 lies on square 2. The second fold puts square 5 on square 2, and square 8 on square 5 (since 8 lay on 5 after the first fold). So the holes are in squares 2, 5, 8 and 11. Their sum is 26.

solve.work: Layers at square 2's place: 2, 11 (13-k), and 5, 8 (from second fold); 2+5+8+11=26.

questions.skill: two folds and a punched sheet
questions.stem: A square sheet has sides of 8 cm. It is folded in half so that its left edge meets its right edge, and then folded in half again so that its bottom edge meets its top edge. A small square of side 4 cm is now in front of you, and two neighbouring sides of it are folds. A hole is punched 1 cm from one fold and 3 cm from the other fold. The sheet is opened out. The four holes are the corners of a rectangle. What is the perimeter of that rectangle in centimetres?
questions.solution: The holes are mirror images across each fold. Across the first fold two holes are 2 x 1 = 2 cm apart, and across the second fold two holes are 2 x 3 = 6 cm apart. The rectangle is 2 cm by 6 cm, so its perimeter is 2 x (2 + 6) = 16 cm.

solve.work: Holes 1 cm either side of one fold line and 3 cm either side of the other: 2 by 6 rectangle, perimeter 16.

questions.stem: A turtle starts on a grid square facing north. It repeats this over and over: walk 3 squares forward, then turn a quarter turn to the right. It does this 6 times in all. What is the smallest number of squares it must walk, along grid lines, to get back to its starting square?
questions.solution: Four repeats make a square walk, which brings the turtle back to the start, facing north. The fifth repeat takes it 3 squares north and the sixth takes it 3 squares east. To get back it needs 3 squares west and 3 squares south, which is 6 squares.

solve.work: N3,E3,S3,W3,N3,E3 ends 3 right and 3 up: 6 squares back.

questions.stem: A paper strip has 9 squares numbered 1 to 9. It is folded like a zig-zag. Squares 1, 2 and 3 lie in a row on the table. The strip folds over between squares 3 and 4, so that squares 4, 5 and 6 lie on top, with 4 directly above 3. It folds over again between squares 6 and 7, so that squares 7, 8 and 9 lie on top of those, with 7 directly above 6. Square 2 has two squares above it in the same pile. What is the sum of the numbers of those three squares?
questions.solution: Square 4 is above 3, so 5 is above 2 and 6 is above 1. Square 7 is above 6, so 8 is above 5 and 9 is above 4. The pile with square 2 is 2, 5 and 8, which add up to 15.

questions.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, and then in half again the other way, to make a small square. One corner of the small square was the centre of the sheet, and the two sides meeting at that corner are folds. A small triangle is cut off that corner by a straight cut joining the two folds at equal distances from the corner. The sheet is opened out. What is the shape of the hole?
choices: a rectangle that is not a square
questions.solution: Opening out gives four copies of the cut-off triangle, one in each quarter of the sheet, all with their right angle at the centre and their short sides along the fold lines. They join up into one hole. Its four corners lie at equal distances from the centre on the fold lines, so it is a square.

solve.work: Cut points at distance d on the folds unfold to (±d,0),(0,±d): a square (diamond).

questions.stem: A beetle starts on a square of a grid. Each move takes it one square right, left, up or down. It moves 2 squares right, then 2 up, then 2 left, then 2 down. How many different squares has it stood on during the whole walk, counting the starting square once?
questions.solution: The walk goes round the edge of a 3 by 3 block of squares and ends where it started. It visits the 8 squares round the edge and never the middle one. So 8 different squares.

solve.work: Walks the ring of a 3x3 block: 8 squares.

questions.stem: A square is made of four equal small squares, two rows of two. In every small square one diagonal is drawn, from its top-left corner to its bottom-right corner. How many triangles of any size can you find, if every side of a triangle must lie along a drawn line?
questions.solution: The 8 small triangles (two in each small square) count. Two diagonals join up into one long line that runs from the top-right corner of the big square to its bottom-left corner. Along that long line, one big triangle sits in the top-left corner and one in the bottom-right corner. That makes 8 + 2 = 10.

solve.work: 8 small triangles; two diagonals line up into the big diagonal giving 2 large ones; all diagonals parallel so no others.

questions.stem: Zoe looks at a wall clock in a mirror. The hands, as she sees them in the mirror, look exactly like a clock showing 4:30 (ignore the numbers). What time is it really?
questions.solution: A mirror swaps left and right, so a hand that points to the 4 position really points to the 8 position, and in general a position p becomes 12 - p. The minute hand is at 6 in both, and the hour hand halfway between 4 and 5 is really halfway between 7 and 8. So the time is 7:30.

solve.work: Left-right mirror: minute hand at 6 stays, hour hand between 4 and 5 becomes between 7 and 8: 7:30 (12:00-4:30).

questions.stem: Two identical squares of paper with sides of 2 cm lie flat on a table. The second square is the first moved 1 cm to the right and 1 cm up, so the two overlap in a small square. How many straight sides does the outline of the whole shape have?
questions.solution: The outline goes along the bottom and right of the first square up to the point where the second square starts, then along the second square, and the same on the other side. It makes a staircase with 8 straight sides.

solve.work: Union of [0,2]^2 and [1,3]^2 has 8 vertices: 8 sides.

questions.stem: A box has 2 layers of small cubes. In each layer the cubes are in 3 rows with 4 cubes in each row. How many cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: Each layer has 3 x 4 = 12 cubes, and there are 2 layers, so 24 cubes.

questions.stem: On a die, the numbers on opposite faces add to 7. A die lies on a table with 5 on its top face. What number is on the face touching the table?
questions.solution: The face opposite 5 is 7 - 5 = 2, and that face is on the table.

questions.skill: perimeter of a rectangle of squares
questions.stem: Six squares with sides of 1 cm are placed edge to edge to make a rectangle with 2 rows of 3 squares. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in centimetres?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 3 cm long and 2 cm wide. Its perimeter is 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.

questions.stem: A straight fence has 6 posts in a row, with 2 metres between each two neighbouring posts. How many metres long is the fence from the first post to the last?
questions.solution: 6 posts have 5 gaps between them. Each gap is 2 metres, so the fence is 5 x 2 = 10 metres.

questions.stem: A cube is made of 8 small cubes, 2 along each edge. Its whole outside is painted red. The cube is then taken apart. How many of the small cubes have exactly 3 red faces?
questions.solution: Every small cube sits at a corner of the big cube. Each meets three outside faces, so all 8 have exactly 3 red faces.

solve.work: Every small cube is a corner: 8.

questions.stem: A carpet is a rectangle 5 metres long and 3 metres wide. A square rug with sides of 2 metres lies on it, completely on the carpet. How many square metres of the carpet are not covered by the rug?
questions.solution: The carpet has area 5 x 3 = 15 square metres and the rug has area 2 x 2 = 4. The uncovered part is 15 - 4 = 11 square metres.

questions.skill: cubes in a tower of layers
questions.stem: A tower is built in three layers of cubes. The bottom layer is a 3 by 3 square of cubes. The middle layer is a 2 by 2 square of cubes sitting on it. The top layer is one cube. How many cubes are used?
questions.solution: The layers have 9, 4 and 1 cubes. Altogether 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.

questions.skill: side of a square from its perimeter
questions.stem: A piece of string 24 cm long is bent into a square with no string left over. How many centimetres long is each side of the square?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides, so each is 24 / 4 = 6 cm.

questions.stem: How many edges does a cube have?
questions.solution: A cube has 4 edges on the top face, 4 on the bottom face and 4 standing between them. That is 12 edges.

questions.skill: faces of a tower of cubes
questions.stem: Three cubes are stacked in a tower on a table, one directly on top of another. How many square faces does the tower have on its outside, not counting the face that touches the table?
