questions.solution: Each of the 3 cubes shows 4 side faces, which is 12 faces. The top cube also shows its top face. That makes 12 + 1 = 13.

questions.stem: A rectangular floor mat is made of tiles, 6 tiles wide and 4 tiles tall. Then a border exactly one tile wide is laid outside the mat, all the way round it, using new tiles. How many new tiles make up the border?
questions.solution: With the border the rectangle is 8 tiles wide and 6 tiles tall, which is 48 tiles. The mat itself uses 24 tiles. The border is 48 - 24 = 24 tiles.

solve.work: Outer rectangle 8 x 6 = 48, minus mat 6 x 4 = 24, gives 24. Check: 2x8 + 2x4 = 24.

questions.stem: A 3 by 3 by 3 cube is built from 27 small cubes. Pat pushes out the 3 small cubes in the middle column, from the top face straight down to the bottom face, to make a tunnel. How many small cubes are left?
questions.solution: Pat removes 3 cubes from the 27, which leaves 24.

questions.stem: On every die the numbers on opposite faces add to 7. Two dice are stacked, one directly on top of the other, on a table. The lower die has 6 on the face touching the table. The upper die has 5 on its top face. You cannot see three faces: the face on the table and the two faces pressed together. What is the sum of the numbers on these three faces?
questions.solution: The lower die's top face is opposite 6, so it shows 1. The upper die's bottom face is opposite 5, so it shows 2. With the 6 on the table the sum is 6 + 1 + 2 = 9.

solve.work: Table face 6; lower top 1; upper bottom 7-5=2; 6+1+2=9.

questions.stem: A square field has sides of 12 metres. Fence posts stand every 3 metres all round the outside, with one post at each corner too. How many posts are there altogether?
questions.solution: The distance all round is 4 x 12 = 48 metres. With a post every 3 metres there are 48 / 3 = 16 posts. Round a closed loop there are as many posts as gaps.

solve.work: Perimeter 48 / 3 = 16 posts on a closed loop.

questions.stem: Squares of side 1 cm are joined edge to edge into an L shape: a column of 4 squares, with 2 more squares in a row to the right of the bottom square of the column, so that the bottom row has 3 squares. What is the perimeter of the L shape in centimetres?
questions.solution: The L fits exactly in a box 3 cm wide and 4 cm tall, and its outline is as long as the outline of that box, because it has no dents that stick inwards beyond the corner. That is 2 x (3 + 4) = 14 cm.

solve.work: L fits a 3 by 4 box with only one inward corner: perimeter 2(3+4)=14; checked by edge count.

questions.stem: Cubes are stacked in nine columns on a 3 by 3 base, with no gaps. Seen from above, the heights of the columns, row by row, are: first row 2, 1, 3; second row 1, 1, 1; third row 3, 2, 1. How many of the cubes cannot be seen from above?
questions.solution: There are 6 + 3 + 6 = 15 cubes in all. The top cube of each of the 9 columns can be seen from above, and the other 15 - 9 = 6 cubes are hidden under them.

questions.stem: A rectangle of paper is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. A smaller rectangle, 3 cm by 2 cm, is cut away from one corner, with its two sides along the sides of the big rectangle. What is the perimeter of the paper that is left, in centimetres?
questions.solution: The cut-out takes away part of two sides but adds a new edge of the same total length, since a notch in a corner keeps the outline as long as the box around it. The perimeter stays 2 x (8 + 5) = 26 cm.

questions.stem: A die lies on a table with 1 on top, 2 facing you and 3 on its right-hand side. Opposite faces add to 7. You tip it over its bottom right edge, a quarter turn to the right, so that it lands on its former right-hand face. What number is on top now?
questions.solution: Tipping to the right brings the left-hand face to the top. The left-hand face is opposite 3, so it shows 7 - 3 = 4.

solve.work: Rolling right brings the left face (7-3=4) to the top.

questions.stem: A garden path is made of 7 flat stones in a row. Each stone is 40 cm long and there is a gap of 20 cm between each two neighbouring stones. How many centimetres long is the path from the start of the first stone to the end of the last stone?
questions.solution: The 7 stones are 7 x 40 = 280 cm long. There are 6 gaps of 20 cm, which is 120 cm. The path is 280 + 120 = 400 cm.

questions.stem: A chain is made of 5 links in a row. Each link is 6 cm long, and each two neighbouring links overlap by 1 cm. How many centimetres long is the whole chain?
questions.solution: The links add up to 5 x 6 = 30 cm. There are 4 overlaps of 1 cm, so the chain is 30 - 4 = 26 cm.

questions.stem: A cube measuring 4 by 4 by 4 is made of 64 small cubes. The whole outside is painted, and then the cube is taken apart. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
questions.solution: Such cubes lie along the edges of the big cube but not at its corners. Each of the 12 edges has 4 small cubes, of which 2 are corners, so 2 are left. That gives 12 x 2 = 24.

questions.stem: A rectangular floor mat is made of tiles and is 3 tiles tall. Then a border exactly one tile wide is laid outside the mat, all the way round it, using 26 new tiles. How many tiles wide is the mat?
questions.solution: If the mat is w tiles wide, the mat with its border has (w + 2) x 5 tiles, and the mat itself has 3w. Their difference is 5w + 10 - 3w = 2w + 10 = 26, so w = 8. Check: 10 x 5 - 8 x 3 = 50 - 24 = 26.

questions.stem: A die lies on a table with 1 on top, 2 facing you and 3 on its right-hand side. Opposite faces add to 7. You tip it a quarter turn to the right, then a quarter turn away from you, then a quarter turn to the right again. What number is on top at the end?
questions.solution: Start: top 1, front 2, right 3, so bottom 6, back 5, left 4. Tipping right gives top 4, front 2, right 1, left 6, back 5. Tipping away from you brings the front to the top: top 2, right 1, left 6. Tipping right brings the left face to the top, so the top is 6.

solve.work: Right: top 4,right 1; away: top 2 (front), right 1, left 6; right: top 6.

questions.stem: Squares of side 1 cm are placed in four rows to make a staircase. The bottom row has 4 squares, the next row 3, the next 2 and the top row 1. All rows start at the same left edge. What is the perimeter of the staircase in centimetres?
questions.solution: The outline of a staircase is as long as the outline of the box around it. The box is 4 cm wide and 4 cm tall, so the perimeter is 2 x (4 + 4) = 16 cm.

solve.work: Staircase perimeter equals its 4 by 4 bounding square: 16.

questions.skill: fence for a pen against a wall
questions.stem: A farmer builds a rectangular pen against a long straight wall, so the wall forms one side and no fence is needed there. The pen is 10 metres along the wall and 6 metres deep. Fence panels are 2 metres long. How many panels are needed?
questions.solution: Three sides need fence: one of 10 metres and two of 6 metres, which is 22 metres in all. The number of panels is 22 / 2 = 11.

questions.skill: outside faces of a stepped tower
questions.stem: A tower is built from small cubes. The bottom layer is a 5 by 5 square of cubes. The layer on it is a 3 by 3 square of cubes in the middle. The top layer is one cube in the middle. All the outside faces except the one touching the table are painted. How many small square faces are painted?
questions.solution: Looking from above, the painted top faces together cover the 5 by 5 base, so there are 25 of them. The four sides show 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 faces each, which is 36. In all 25 + 36 = 61.

questions.stem: A square sheet of card has sides of 8 cm. A square of side 2 cm is cut from each corner. The four flaps are folded up to make a box with no lid. How many cubes of edge 1 cm fit exactly inside the box?
questions.solution: The base of the box is 8 - 2 - 2 = 4 cm by 4 cm, and the sides stand 2 cm high. The box holds 4 x 4 x 2 = 32 cubes.

questions.stem: A 3 by 3 square is made of 9 unit squares of side 1 cm. The four corner squares are taken away, leaving a plus shape of 5 squares. What is the perimeter of the plus in centimetres?
questions.solution: The plus has 4 arms. Each arm has an end of 1 cm and two sides of 1 cm, which is 3 cm of outline. That is 4 x 3 = 12 cm.

solve.work: Each of the 4 arms contributes 3 edges: 12.

questions.stem: A framework is made of wire along every edge of all the small cubes in a 3 by 3 by 3 cube, which is built from 27 small cubes with edges of 1 cm. Where two small cubes share an edge there is only one piece of wire. How many centimetres of wire is that in all?
questions.solution: Take the wires that run left to right. There are 4 positions up and down and 4 positions front to back, so 16 such wires, each 3 cm long, which is 48 cm. The wires in each of the other two directions are the same. So 3 x 48 = 144 cm.

solve.work: Per direction 4x4=16 lines of 3 cm = 48; x3 directions = 144.

questions.stem: Two cubes with edges of 2 cm are glued together face to face, one directly on top of the other, to make a block 2 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm. What is the area of the whole outside of the block, in square centimetres?
questions.solution: The block has two ends of 2 x 2 = 4 square cm and four long sides of 2 x 4 = 8 square cm. That is 2 x 4 + 4 x 8 = 8 + 32 = 40.
